A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIO-VQA, RIO-Bench and RIO-RT work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original LVLM evaluations, defense comparisons, LoRA ablations, attention analyses and cross-dataset generalization results, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SceneTAP evaluations, a human audit, and modern/frontier-model experiments.

M1.justification: RIO-RT retains its balanced SFT/LoRA procedure. Benchmark construction adds an adapted SceneTAP insertion branch with OCR-preserving masks and placement fallbacks. Appendix A.2 also revises the described negative-label selection through CLIP-filtered exclusions, ancestor exclusion and a training-vocabulary restriction.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation-only SceneTAP conditions for object MC/OE and text OE, extending digital-overlay testing to scene-coherent generative insertions. The underlying TextVQA/Open Images coverage and external Typo-D, AI2D, ChartQA, DocVQA and InfoVQA evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Direct comparisons against RIO-RT retain the original models, CoT and IT-RT on the same six backbones. v2 Table 5 separately evaluates additional unmodified LVLMs for capability and scaling; it does not introduce another competing defense into the RIO-RT comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated placement grid from 7×7 to 11×11 and overlap-resampling limit from 100 to 200. New protocols include the four-stratum human audit and frontier/scaling evaluations averaging hard-overlay and SceneTAP scores. Appendix B also revises scoring descriptions. These documented changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a 400-sample audit of answerability and distractor validity, tests transfer from overlay-only training to unseen SceneTAP attacks, and analyzes model scaling. New qualitative SceneTAP cases accompany these tests. Existing LoRA-placement, attention, external-dataset and training-data-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new audit introduces three-annotator reliability reporting, including raw agreement of 90.0–94.3% and Gwet’s AC1 of 0.89–0.94. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run uncertainty or confidence intervals for model performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds SceneTAP, audit and frontier/scaling results. Table 5 reports GPT-5.4 object accuracy of 96.4 clean versus 74.3 attacked, and Gemini-2.5-Pro at 96.1 versus 77.7. Retained entries also change, such as original LLaVA-1.5-7B object-clean accuracy from 93.5 to 93.7. Expanded attack averages are not directly comparable with v1’s overlay-only averages.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces v1’s leave-one-annotator-out TextVQA formula with min(matching answers/3, 1), which is mathematically different for partial agreement. The explicit multi-label CLIP-M definition is also omitted in favor of a single-ground-truth formulation. The R-CLIP-M subtraction principle remains; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central task, counterfactual benchmark and robustness–reading trade-off claims remain. However, v2 narrows RIO-RT from a novel defense acquiring a new capability to a minimal reference baseline, explicitly making benchmarking the primary contribution and claiming largely preserved reading performance.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies causal and applicability claims: vision-only defenses are no longer described as inherently incompatible with reading, and cross-dataset transfer is described more cautiously. Limitations now include incomplete typography/threat-model coverage and the fixed SFT recipe and budget. SceneTAP results receive a new interpretation as transfer beyond training-time overlays.

D1.justification: v2 specifies AdamW and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and documents SceneTAP masks, fallbacks, components and computational costs. Conversely, it removes some exact OCR-matching details, the smallest-index QA-selection rule, the project-page pointer and the explicit code-release promise. These are documentation changes, not evidence that external resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gwet’s reliability reference and removes the general adversarial-attack references by Brown, Goodfellow and Madry. Most related work remains, including the previously cited SceneTAP. Positioning becomes more restrained, presenting RIO-RT as a complementary baseline rather than a fundamentally novel alternative to prior defenses.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, benchmark explanations and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten around relevant scene text versus inserted distractors. Appendix descriptions are substantially condensed and reorganized, alongside new audit and frontier-evaluation sections. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column layout, merges v1 Figures 1–2, expands result tables with SceneTAP columns, and adds audit/frontier tables and a SceneTAP qualitative figure. Appendix Figures 6–11 gain SceneTAP panels and several corrected question labels. Retained attention and data-size plots are largely redisplayed.

improvement.justification: The 400-sample human audit directly addresses v1’s lack of empirical validation for automated benchmark construction, while unseen SceneTAP tests strengthen evidence beyond digital overlays. Frontier evaluations and more restrained claims further improve relevance and calibration. These substantial gains outweigh reporting regressions: metric descriptions lose precision, and Table 6 retains 34,826 evaluation samples although its expanded rows sum to 44,324, weakening reproducibility.
